title: Gibbs Sampling
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Gibbs sampling updates each variable from its full conditional given the others.
long: Sample from conditionals in turn. Special case of Metropolis Hastings.

title: Importance Sampling Estimator
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Importance sampling estimates expectations under p using weighted samples from proposal q.
long: Reweight easier samples. High variance if proposal misses target.

title: Particle Filter
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A particle filter approximates filtering distributions by propagating and resampling weighted samples.
short: Sequential Monte Carlo for state estimation.
long: Sequential Monte Carlo for state estimation. Resampling avoids weight collapse.

title: Beta Binomial Conjugacy
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A beta prior on a Bernoulli parameter yields a beta posterior after binomial data.
long: Conjugacy keeps the family. Multiply prior by likelihood.

title: Dirichlet Multinomial Conjugacy
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A Dirichlet prior is conjugate to a multinomial likelihood.
long: Counts update parameters. Multiply densities and collect powers.

title: Collider Explaining Away
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Conditioning on a common effect can induce dependence between independent causes.
long: Observing an effect links causes. Colliders must not be conditioned on naively.

title: Belief Propagation
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Belief propagation passes messages between nodes to compute marginals on factor graphs.
long: Message passing for tree inference. Loopy graphs are approximate.

title: Junction Tree Algorithm
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Junction tree performs exact inference by clustering variables into a clique tree.
long: Cost exponential in treewidth. Triangulate then build clique tree.

title: Loopy Belief Propagation
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Running belief propagation on cyclic graphs often works well without general exactness.
latex: \text{loopy fixed points need not be exact marginals}
long: A practical approximation with caveats. Exactness holds on trees.

title: MCMC Mixing Time
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: MCMC bias decreases as the chain approaches stationarity at a rate governed by mixing time.
long: Longer runs reduce bias. Multimodal targets mix slowly.

title: Conditional Random Field
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A CRF models labels given observations with an undirected graphical model.
long: Discriminative structured prediction. Avoids modelling p(x).

title: Latent Variable Model
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A latent variable model uses unobserved variables to explain dependence among observations.
long: Hidden structure explains data. Latents not identified without assumptions.

title: MCMC versus Variational Inference
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: MCMC is asymptotically exact but slow while variational inference is fast but biased by family choice.
short: Sampling exact in limit VI approximate.
long: Sampling exact in limit VI approximate. Practical comparison not a theorem.

title: Jensen Inequality for Log Likelihood
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Concavity of log yields a lower bound on log marginal likelihood.
long: Concavity gives ELBO. Apply Jensen to log expectation.

title: Amortized Inference
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Amortized inference uses a learned function to output variational parameters per example.
long: Share inference across examples. Trades accuracy for speed.

title: Tokenization
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Tokenization splits text into units such as words subwords or characters.
long: Break text into model units. Choice affects vocabulary and rare words.

title: Byte Pair Encoding
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: BPE builds a subword vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent symbol pair.
long: Grow vocabulary by frequent merges. Handles unseen words by composition.
proof: Count adjacent pairs and merge greedily.

title: WordPiece
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: WordPiece merges pairs chosen by likelihood gain rather than raw frequency.
long: Likelihood driven subword merging. Similar in spirit to BPE.

title: Subword Vocabulary Trade Off
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Smaller vocabularies handle rare words better but yield longer sequences.
long: Balance vocabulary against length. Engineering trade off not a theorem.

title: Distributional Hypothesis
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Words in similar contexts tend to have similar meanings.
short: Know a word by its company.
long: Know a word by its company. Linguistic hypothesis behind embeddings.

title: Dense Embeddings versus One Hot
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Dense embeddings encode similarity while one hot vectors treat all words as equally distant.
long: Embeddings encode meaning geometrically. Similarity is learned from context.

title: Word2Vec Skip Gram
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Skip gram learns embeddings by predicting surrounding words from a centre word.
long: Predict context from a word. Negative sampling makes it cheap.
proof: Train shallow net on moving windows.

title: Continuous Bag of Words
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: CBOW predicts the centre word from its surrounding context.
long: Predict a word from neighbours. Inverse of skip gram.

title: GloVe
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: GloVe learns embeddings by factorizing global co occurrence statistics with weighted least squares.
long: Global counts matter. Combines count and prediction ideas.

title: Contextual Embeddings
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Contextual models assign different vectors to the same word in different sentences.
short: A word meaning depends on context.
long: A word meaning depends on context. Architectural advance over static vectors.
